from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Shrinking Interval (The Intuitive Limit)", [
            "Move the second point closer to the first.",
            "The secant line becomes a tangent line.",
            "As the interval shrinks, we find instantaneous speed."
        ])
        
        # Setup Graph
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 4, 1], y_range=[0, 4, 1], axis_config={"include_tip": True}).scale(0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(axes, 'D3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.add(axes)
        
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.25 * x**2, x_range=[0, 4], color=BLUE)
        self.add(curve)
        
        p1 = Dot(axes.c2p(1, 0.25), color=WHITE)
        p2_start = axes.c2p(3, 2.25)
        p2 = Dot(p2_start, color="#32CD32")
        
        secant = Line(p1.get_center(), p2.get_center(), color=YELLOW)
        
        self.add(p1, p2, secant)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#32CD32")
        
        # Move p2 closer to p1
        p2_target = axes.c2p(1.2, 0.25 * 1.2**2)
        
        # Use ValueTracker for smooth animation
        t = ValueTracker(3.0)
        
        secant.add_updater(lambda mob: mob.put_start_and_end_on(
            p1.get_center(),
            axes.c2p(t.get_value(), 0.25 * t.get_value()**2)
        ))
        
        p2.add_updater(lambda mob: mob.move_to(
            axes.c2p(t.get_value(), 0.25 * t.get_value()**2)
        ))
        
        self.play(t.animate.set_value(1.2), run_time=3)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        # Continue moving closer until tangent
        self.play(t.animate.set_value(1.01), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF4500")
        # Final shrink
        self.play(t.animate.set_value(1.001), run_time=1)
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Clean up updaters
        secant.remove_updater(secant.get_updaters()[0])
        p2.remove_updater(p2.get_updaters()[0])

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "The derivative is a formal mathematical limit.",
            "Slope of tangent equals the derivative at x.",
            "It measures steepness at a single precise point."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Defining the Derivative", lecture_lines)
        
        # --- Pre-define objects ---
        # 1. Limit definition
        limit_formula = MathTex(
            r"f'(x) = \lim_{h \to 0} \frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}",
            color="#FFD700"
        )
        self.place_at_grid(limit_formula, 'B2', scale_factor=1.2)
        
        # 2. Tangent line visual
        # Using simple axes and function as a visual representation
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-1, 3], y_range=[-1, 3], axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: x**2, color=BLUE)
        tangent_line = Line(start=LEFT*1, end=RIGHT*1, color=WHITE)
        point_a = Dot(color=RED)
        
        visual_group = VGroup(axes, curve, tangent_line, point_a)
        self.place_in_area(visual_group, 'D1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        self.play(Write(limit_formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        # Highlighting derivative notation in the formula
        self.play(Indicate(limit_formula[0][0:4]))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#ADD8E6"))
        self.play(Create(visual_group))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Application: Prediction and Dynamics", [
            "Derivatives show change at an exact instant.",
            "They are essential for predicting dynamic motion.",
            "Use them to optimize paths like rocket launches."
        ])
        
        # Define Path and Objects
        curve = FunctionGraph(lambda t: 0.1 * (t**3 - 3*t), x_range=[-2, 2], color=GRAY)
        self.place_in_area(curve, 'B2', 'E5')
        
        dot = Dot(color=YELLOW)
        dot.move_to(curve.point_from_proportion(0))
        
        velocity_vector = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*0.5, color="#00FFFF")
        tangent_line = Line(start=LEFT*1, end=RIGHT*1, color="#FFA500")

        # Tracker for position on curve
        t = ValueTracker(0)
        
        def update_objects(m):
            prop = t.get_value()
            pos = curve.point_from_proportion(prop)
            dot.move_to(pos)
            
            # Derivative calculation (approximate slope)
            delta = 0.01
            p1 = curve.point_from_proportion(max(0, prop - delta))
            p2 = curve.point_from_proportion(min(1, prop + delta))
            tangent_dir = p2 - p1
            tangent_dir /= np.linalg.norm(tangent_dir)
            
            velocity_vector.put_start_and_end_on(pos, pos + tangent_dir * 0.8)
            tangent_line.put_start_and_end_on(pos - tangent_dir * 0.5, pos + tangent_dir * 0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.add(curve, dot)
        self.play(Create(curve), FadeIn(dot))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FFFF")
        
        dot.add_updater(update_objects)
        velocity_vector.add_updater(update_objects)
        self.add(velocity_vector)
        self.play(t.animate.set_value(1), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFA500")
        
        tangent_line.add_updater(update_objects)
        self.add(tangent_line)
        self.play(t.animate.set_value(0), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        
        self.wait(1)

outline.topic: From Average Speed to Instantaneous Rate of Change: Understanding the Derivative

sections.title: The Problem of Average Speed
sections.content: Introduce the concept of average speed over an interval using the slope formula (rise/run). Visualize this on a position-time graph as a secant line connecting two points.
sections.example: A cheetah running: If it covers 100 meters in 5 seconds, its average speed is 20 m/s, but it didn't run at exactly that speed the whole time.

sections.title: The Shrinking Interval (The Intuitive Limit)
sections.content: Animate the second point on the graph moving closer to the first. Show the secant line morphing into a tangent line. Explain that as the time interval Δt approaches 0, the average speed becomes instantaneous speed.
sections.example: A GPS tracker on a race car: As you reduce the measurement interval from 1 second to 0.1s to 0.001s, the calculated speed converges to the speedometer reading at that exact moment.

sections.title: Defining the Derivative
sections.content: Formalize the concept using the limit notation: f'(x) = lim(h→0) [f(x+h) - f(x)] / h. Connect this algebra back to the visual 'slope of the tangent line' at a single point.
sections.example: Representing the curve as a path: The slope of the tangent line at any point on the curve represents the 'steepness' or rate of change of the function at that precise coordinate.

sections.title: Application: Prediction and Dynamics
sections.content: Summarize that the derivative tells us how a quantity changes at an exact instant. This is the foundation for predicting motion and optimization.
sections.example: A rocket launch: The derivative of its height function gives us the instantaneous velocity at any second, allowing engineers to know exactly when to trigger stage separation.
